To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed monoclonal antibodies reactive against the BAF155 and closely related BAF170 subunits of human SWI/ SNF complexes.
monoclonal antibodies were developed that are reactive against BAF155 and/or BAF170.
the DXD7 and DXD12 monoclonal antibodies are specific for the human SMARCC1 and SMARCC2 proteins, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of monoclonal antibodies against the BAF155 and the BAF170 components of human SW/SNF-related complexes.
the isolation of monoclonal antibodies against the BAF155 and closely related BAF170 proteins.
the use of monoclonal antibodies for immunopreciptation and Western blotting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these monoclonal antibodies recognize BAF155 and, in the case of DXD12, also BAF170.
the DXD7 antibody recognizes the BAF155 protein and the DXD12 antibody recognizes the BAH155 and BAH170 proteins.
the DXD7 antibody reacts specifically with BAF155, and the DXD12 antibody reacts with BAF155 and a BAF155-related protein (BAF170) which has a high degree of amino acid sequence similarity to BAF155.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antibodies are useful for studying the role of BAF155 and related proteins in transcriptional controls.
we have developed a panel of antibodies to BAF155 and related proteins, which should facilitate the analysis of the SWI/SNF complexes.
we have developed a set of antibodies that are useful for the analysis of the SWI/SNF family of proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
monoclonal antibodies specific for the BAF155 subunit are now available.
monoclonal antibodies reactive against a BAF subunit are available for the first time.
the DXD12 antibody can be used to detect the presence of BAF155 and/or BAF170 in a variety of biological samples.
